# Currency and Costs

*Generated by `src/currency.py`. Rates are read from the stored World Bank file; nothing is typed in.*

## Three ways to talk about price

| measure | unit | comparable across countries? | used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `price_range` (1-4) | Zomato price band | **Yes** (currency-free) | default for all cross-country comparisons, model feature |
| `avg_cost_for_two` | local currency (see `currency`) | **No** | within one country only (e.g. India in INR), recommender budgets |
| `cost_pct_in_country` | percentile 0-1 among restaurants of the same country and currency | **Yes** (relative position) | model feature; 0 = cheapest, 1 = dearest in that country |
| `avg_cost_for_two_usd` | US dollars, **approximate** | Yes, roughly | charts that compare cost levels across countries |

## Exchange rates used (approximate)

Source: World Bank, World Development Indicators, PA.NUS.FCRF Official exchange rate (LCU per US$, period average), 2017; downloaded 2026-11-19. Raw file stored unchanged: `data/raw/worldbank_PA.NUS.FCRF_official_exchange_rate.csv`; table used: `data/processed/exchange_rates_2017.csv`.

Why approximate: the rate is a 2017 annual average, and the date when Zomato listed each price is not in the data (the dataset was published in 2018). Use USD values for broad comparisons only.

The currency label `Dollar($)` is used for the United States, Australia, Canada and Singapore. It is taken to be each country's own dollar, so rates are matched by country, not by currency label.

| country | currency code | World Bank name | local units per US$ (2017) |

| India | INR | India | 65.1216 |
| United States | USD | United States | 1.0000 |
